text:
PROPOSAL C, and first a SECOND GHOST found by the same derivation as the parked branch.

THE RECORD ON THIS BEAD SAYS: "C becomes actionable once Semantic joins MayBeMissing on
bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9." DERIVED FROM WHAT LANDED: Semantic did NOT join MayBeMissing and now
never will. Today's ruling was the opposite - Semantic is PRICED, so putting it in missingTerms
would make the record internally false, and scout was explicit that a term which is both present and
weight-bearing cannot be called missing. It joined a NEW carrier, imputedTerms, with its own policy
set MayBeImputed. So the stated precondition cannot be satisfied as written; read literally this
bead waits forever. C IS UNBLOCKED, by a different mechanism than the one it was waiting for. Same
shape as m1/parked-dent: a status that reads as blocked and derives as ready.

WHAT A CELL NOW CARRIES, which is what makes C answerable at all. After today the (unit, node) cell
holds:
  terms          what was measured, per dimension
  missingTerms   what was absent and contributed nothing
  imputedTerms   what was PRICED FROM A CONSTANT, with the provider's MissingReason
  supportWeight  the share of ELIGIBLE weight actually measured
  reductions     StructuralReductionReceipt: member identities, excluded members with their
                 contradictions, the reducer, and observed-estimate coverage
  sourceChartCoverage
Those five were not all there this morning. The cell can now say not just what it scored but which
dimensions it could not score and why, and that is the difference between a number and a trace.

THE TEXTUAL COORDINATES ARE ALREADY ON BOTH SIDES, which is the part I had not checked before:
  RecallUnit.span : SpanSet  and RecallUnit.text  - the recall-side words
  NodeSummary.support : SpanSet                   - exact evidence in the source text
So "which words support this alignment cell" is not a new artifact to invent. It is a JOIN that
nobody has written down: unit.span on the transcript, node.support on the source, and the per-term
breakdown explaining what each dimension contributed and what it could not.

PROPOSAL C, concretely:
  A cell trace is a FUNCTION, not a stored artifact - trace(unit, node, breakdown, view) - returning
  the recall spans, the source spans, and per CostTerm one of {Measured(value), Absent(reason),
  Imputed(constant, reason), Ineligible}. Nothing is persisted, so nothing can drift from the cell
  it describes; it recomputes from the breakdown that is already carried in HsmmResult and already
  round-trips through hsmm/v3.

WHICH MODULE OWNS IT - the bead's actual question. `align`, not `recall`. The trace needs
CostBreakdown, CostTerm, the eligibility notion and the reduction receipts, all of which are
align-internal; recall knows nothing about cells. Recall's contribution is already discharged by
RecallUnit.span and .text. Putting it in recall would invert the dependency and force half of
align's vocabulary into a module whose subject is transcripts.

THE FOURTH CASE IS THE ONE I WOULD ARGUE ABOUT. Measured / Absent / Imputed are all recorded on the
cell today. INELIGIBLE IS NOT - eligibility is computed inside cost() and thrown away, so a reader
cannot currently distinguish "we could not measure this" from "this cell never had this dimension".
That is the distinction scout drew for dProp/dEnt and the one I fixed twice today in chartEligible
and structuralEligible. C either needs the eligible set carried on the breakdown, or it can only
offer three cases and must say so. I lean to carrying it - it is one Set[CostTerm] and it makes the
supportWeight denominator inspectable rather than implicit - but that is an estimand-adjacent
addition to a public carrier, so it is a ruling, not my call.

NOT PROPOSING A CANDIDATE. Two of mine are already queued on the merge gate and one of them touches
CostBreakdown, so a third would collide. Recording the design so the bead stops being sequenced
behind a precondition that can never occur.
